task: P3 held-out anomaly-tail preservation test (R9 in-sample-scoring item)
statistic: tail-to-bulk contrast R = p99/p50; preservation ratio rho = R_heldout / R_insample
result: Held-out tail preservation PASSES: across all 5 folds the anomaly-defining upper-tail contrast (p99/p50) computed on 47,000 DESI rows the model provably never trained on is preserved relative to the in-sample scoring distribution (mean rho=1.00, min rho=0.94 >= 0.5 gate; 3/5 folds rho>=1, i.e. the held-out tail is AT LEAST as sharp as in-sample). The top-1% DESI anomaly population is not an in-sample-inflation artifact: its defining tail survives on genuinely unseen data.
honest_bound: This is a distributional (percentile-level) held-out test on committed summaries, not a per-object held-out re-score of the full 22.5M-spectrum released catalog — the raw per-object native score parquets live on an exited pod and are not in the committed tree or HF release. It complements, and is consistent with, the committed 5-fold per-object Jaccard stability (mean J=0.862) and the Planck held-out membership test (1.6x over-representation, p=5.5e-4). All three are out-of-sample and all three pass; a full per-object held-out re-inference of the released headline catalog remains pod-blocked and is disclosed as such.
